evidence: Patch applies: generated tree differs from base only in src/textual/app.py and new tests/test_call_from_thread.py (checks.json patch_applies=true).

checks.json candidate_tests: returncode -9, 'Timed out after 600s'. The reference_tests phase passed, but the venv's textual.pth points at reference/src (venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/textual.pth), so that pass does not show the candidate source passes.

Reproduced in a scratch copy with the candidate src/ first on sys.path: tests/test_concurrency.py::test_call_from_thread_app_not_running passes; tests/test_concurrency.py::test_call_from_thread hangs (timeout, rc=124).

Root cause, from a probe run against candidate src: the worker-thread callback raises NoActiveAppError in textual/message_pump.py:99-101 via widgets/_text_log.py:94 (TextLog.write -> self.app). The background thread dies, so app.exit is never delivered and app.run() never returns.

Candidate generated/src/textual/app.py:450-454 run_callback() calls the callback without self._set_active(). Reference reference/src/textual/app.py:649 sets the active app inside its run_callback for exactly this reason.
criteria.deficiency: FAIL_TO_PASS test tests/test_concurrency.py::test_call_from_thread hangs against the candidate: a callback that touches a widget (self.app.query_one(TextLog).write) cannot resolve the active app, and the thread-submitted task does not inherit it. The candidate's own tests never touch widgets, so they miss this.

evidence: call_from_thread is defined on App in generated/src/textual/app.py:428-456, next to exit(), the same module as the reference (reference/src/textual/app.py:614).
State attributes are initialised in App.__init__ at generated app.py:271-272.

Loop/thread state is set in App._process_messages at generated app.py:1364-1366, not run() as in the reference (reference/src/textual/app.py:937-938). This is an acceptable alternative: _process_messages is also the entry point used by run_async and the test harness (base app.py:777 and :842).
The new test file is placed under tests/ following the repo's test_*.py convention.
Name and parameters match the reference: call_from_thread(callback, *args, **kwargs) (generated app.py:428; reference app.py:614-618).
Return and callback typing are weaker than the reference, which uses a TypeVar and Callable[..., T | Awaitable[T]] (reference app.py:614-618). Generated app.py:428 uses Callable and -> Any.

Not-running contract: reference raises RuntimeError('App is not running') when the loop is absent (reference app.py:638). The candidate raises a RuntimeError at generated app.py:445-447, but its message says 'must be called from a different thread than the app', which misdescribes the not-running case.

After shutdown the contract fails: no code in generated app.py ever resets _loop (grep finds no '_loop = None'). In a probe, after app.run() returned, call_from_thread on a worker thread blocked: the thread was still alive after 5s and no exception was raised. The reference clears _loop and _thread_id in a finally (reference app.py:937-938), so it raises.
The docstring at generated app.py:429-443 documents only the same-thread RuntimeError, not the not-running case.
criteria.deficiency: The public method's not-running and post-shutdown behaviour does not meet the contract. It raises a misleading message when the app is not running, and it blocks forever after the app has stopped instead of raising.

evidence: No new imports: the candidate uses threading, inspect and asyncio, all already imported in the base app.py (base app.py:4, 9 and the asyncio import).
No new cross-module dependency is introduced in the patch (patch.diff touches only app.py and the new test file).
The reference adds no registration, interface or plugin hook for call_from_thread (reference/src/textual/app.py:614-649), so none is required.
The candidate adds none and needs none.
patch.diff adds no packages, lockfile changes or new third-party imports.
Only stdlib modules already used by app.py are referenced (asyncio, inspect, threading).
call_from_thread belongs on the App class, which owns the running loop; the candidate places it at generated app.py:428-456.

Loop/thread state is set from the app's own message-processing entry point (generated app.py:1364-1366), which the reference's run() placement does not cover. The candidate's placement is therefore a reasonable variant.
Lifecycle teardown is missing; that defect is recorded under abstraction_integrity and api_contract, not here.

The existing active-app mechanism is App._set_active() (base app.py:458-460). The reference uses it inside each callback (reference app.py:649). The candidate never calls it inside run_callback (generated app.py:450-454), so it bypasses the mechanism.

The repo already has an invoke() helper in textual/_callback.py, imported in app.py:44. The reference uses it (reference app.py:~650, 'return await invoke(callback_with_args)'). The candidate reimplements the await logic inline with inspect.isawaitable (generated app.py:452-453) instead of reusing invoke().
criteria.deficiency: The candidate skips the existing active-app mechanism for callbacks and duplicates the existing invoke() helper with an inline reimplementation.

evidence: Widgets resolve their app through the active_app context var (textual/message_pump.py:99-101). Callbacks submitted from another thread therefore lose the app context, because the candidate's run_callback (generated app.py:450-454) never sets it. Probe: NoActiveAppError raised from TextLog.write.

Runtime state is not torn down. _loop and _thread_id are set (generated app.py:1365-1366) and never cleared, so the App keeps a stale loop reference after run() returns. The reference clears them in a finally block (reference app.py:937-938).
criteria.deficiency: The thread-to-app boundary is broken: thread-submitted callbacks run without the app context that the framework expects, and the app keeps stale cross-thread state after shutdown.

evidence: Error messages: the reference uses a specific not-running message (reference app.py:638, 'App is not running'). The candidate's single combined check at generated app.py:445-447 reports the same-thread message for both cases.

Docstring: the candidate's docstring (generated app.py:429-443) is in the repo's Google-style Args/Raises/Returns format, which is acceptable. It omits the not-running Raises case that the reference documents.
Helper reuse: the repo convention is to route callbacks through the invoke() helper (app.py:44), which the candidate does not use (see extension_point_adherence).
criteria.deficiency: The not-running error is misleading and undocumented, and the callback-invocation path diverges from the existing invoke() convention.

evidence: Intent: a background thread can run a callback in the app's loop, get its result or exception back, and must not run from the app thread. The candidate meets the result/exception and same-thread checks; my scratch run passes the candidate's own 3 tests (tests/test_call_from_thread.py, 3 passed).

The reference FAIL_TO_PASS test tests/test_concurrency.py::test_call_from_thread hangs with the candidate source (timeout, rc=124). Its callback writes to a TextLog, which fails because the app context is missing (see patch_and_checks).
After the app stops, call_from_thread blocks indefinitely instead of raising. Probe: worker thread still alive after 5s, no exception raised.

The candidate's added tests never touch widgets or the post-shutdown state, so they do not cover the failing behaviour. They pass with candidate source but hang under the venv's default reference/src path, which is the recorded timeout.
criteria.deficiency: The feature does not behave as required when callbacks touch the app's widgets, and it hangs rather than erroring after the app stops. Both defects are reproduced.
